Two-Player campaign in Halo, clearing rooms in Rainbow Six Vegas, taking on Sweet Tooth in Twisted Metal. What are some of your favorite Co-Op memories?
What are some of your favorite Co-Op memories?

My friend and I were playing some Rainbow six vegas 2. I can't for the life of me be stealthy in that game. I don't know, I just can't. My friend can be stealthy. This guy has started a trend among my friends of being called an Ignorance Cannon. It's kind of like the glass cannon metaphor, but it's because of his particular ability to be ignored within a game.

So, general strategy since I can't sneak past AI in that game, he usually scopes out the room. Spawns can be pretty repetitive in that game, so we always try to switch up levels to slow down our ability to distinctly remember spawns.

So, he scopes out the first room. See's nothing. He continues in, I am waiting patiently for something, anything. He makes it into the second room. Now, this is a house full of dudes. Dudes everywhere. It's a small map with like 45 enemies going to spawn in it. It should be impossible for him to make it into 2 rooms without spotting or being spotted. I mean, they spawn when you walk up to a door for a room.

Well, so he's about to go upstairs.. some shenanigans like 4 rooms deep now, hasn't seen a thing. I finally turn over to look at what he's doing since I've been waiting to just open up all gung-ho. I notice a guy off center of his screen. We argue for a minute that it's a dude, not a statue. He then says, how can it be a dude. I'm in the middle of the room, he'd be shooting at me. So he lifts his gun, shoots the guy in the face. Suddenly All hell breaks loose, for me. I'm hucking grenades, throwing out ammo faster than a politician with excuses.

Well, I finally make it into the first room, from getting pressure from behind. Couldn't find cover, finally die. Now my friend, he's shot some things... I think, but he's now upstairs. He spots a guy, sprays and completely misses with his big ol machinegun. He starts reloading in the open. This AI looks at him (I'm dead btw, so I have nothing else to do but watch this happen) and then looks at the floor and starts shooting.

My friend finally kills him and it dawns on us what he was doing. He was shooting the floor, at where I was.

FFFFFFFF btw, this friend of mine was playing pac-man at an arcade. I saw him start moving into a corner, with 2 ghosts. It's a bad move, but he might still make it. He instead turns and guns it for one of the ghosts. He clips through the ghost and just keeps going.

That's like one of 4 cardinal rules for pac-man. Ghosts kill you on contact. Duh fuq.

My brother is the big thinker of the group and I'm learning to defer to him about overall strategy since he sees the big picture. My other friend is the aggro sponge and can't stealth, but does a great job of suppressing enemies in whatever we play. It's a great feeling to be working with a team and knowing that no one of us is as good as all of us.

Why do websites/apps/games tell me to check my internet connection if they are down
Because they are not anticipating their website or service to be down. They think it is usually an issue with the user.
It is a very simple thing to check that accounts for a huge amount of common issues.

Usually their software isn't smart enough to tell the difference between a server that isn't responding, and a server it can't reach.

The code might look like

Try
{
 getDataFromServer();
}
catch
{
 tellUserToFixInternet();
}

Which from a programmer's perspective is approximately correct behavior, and it usually gets left this way because it's pretty hard for a piece of software to diagnose end to end connectivity problems.
